suggestions.assertion: Does NOT use @media queries for basic responsiveness (wa-flank handles it)
suggestions.reason: This assertion passes even though wa-flank was not used, making it a weak signal. An output with zero responsive behavior (hardcoded 240px sidebar) passes because it technically has no @media queries. The assertion is too easy to satisfy by omission. Consider reformulating as 'Layout responsiveness comes from wa-flank, not @media queries' to require the positive behavior, not just the absence of the negative.

suggestions.assertion: Uses className (not class) on all elements
suggestions.reason: This is a low-signal assertion for a baseline (without_skill) test. Any competent LLM producing React JSX will use className by default. It would only discriminate if the skill were introducing raw wa-* web component elements where 'class' is correct. For a without_skill baseline, it is nearly guaranteed to pass regardless of quality.

No assertion checks whether the output actually provides responsive sidebar behavior (collapse, overlay, or hide on narrow viewports). The hardcoded 240px sidebar will break on mobile. This is the core value of wa-flank that the output missed, but only the wa-flank class name is asserted, not the responsive outcome.

eval_feedback.overall: The core discriminating assertions (wa-flank usage, wa-align-items-stretch, wa-stack/split with justify) correctly failed -- this is a good baseline showing what an LLM produces without the skill. The @media assertion is too permissive and the className assertion is not discriminating for React code.
